notes.title: January Patch
notes.content:
[h3]Mesdames et Messieurs, Ladies and Gentlemen!

Beware as the new patch to your beloved The Amazing American Circus will premiere today!
The new year brings fixes to what was broken, some brand new features, and a promise of a BIG new features coming later this month.[/h3]

[h3]Fixes:

Fixed all not unlocking achievements.
Fixed wrong colors of "Blessed Be Thy Chicken" reward chicken.
Clown's card  “French Drop" now counts all cards in the Players hand correctly.
Fixed Conjoined Twins special effect not being applied on Player's troupe.[/h3]

[h3]Important! Due to an internal error, we had changed save files localization in the last patch. If you have played recently and want to keep your progress - follow the below steps. If you haven’t played before 17th December - your save files should work fine. [/h3]

Locate your save files in C:\Users\<your username>\AppData\LocalLow\Klabater\The Amazing American Circus
Locate files with .dat extension (save0.dat, save1.dat, save2.dat)
Select and move those files to the ‘Saves’ folder. (C:\Users\<your username>\AppData\LocalLow\Klabater\The Amazing American Circus\Saves)
Make sure that the ‘Saves’ folder contains fogOfWarX.png files. 

[h3]New features:
Adjustable speed of animation[/h3]

You can now adjust the speed of animations played when casting cards and finales. We received many requests to add this feature to make The Amazing American Circus gameplay faster and smoother, and now we are delighted to confirm - we did it! You can access this feature in the game settings menu and use a  toolbar “Performance speed” to control animation speed, increasing them by 100% to 200%. The speed can be adjusted in any way anytime during the game.

[h3]More new features coming! [/h3]

The below features are currently “work-in-progress.” However, we expect to make them available as a beta branch to You all for testing still in January. We deliver them in late January or early February if met with positive feedback, so stay tuned for the following announcement coming ETA mid-January.

[h3]Randomized starting troupe[/h3]

When starting a new game, your troupe of artists will be composed randomly within predefined criteria. This will allow more fantastic replayability and encourage players to experiment with a wider choice of artists.

[h3]Artist’s stress effect[/h3]

After every given show based on the show outcome, one of the performing artists can receive the ‘Stressed’ effect. ‘Stress’ will make the artist unable to participate in the next show until the effect is not removed/ cured. The main goal of the feature is to encourage the rotation of the troupe members between the shows.

[h3]Perform Shows in the cities (endlessly)[/h3]

After performing max 3 stars in any city, You still would be able to perform there regularly (including cooldown between shows).

[h3]Steam Cloud Saves[/h3]

Self-explanatory, support of Steam Cloud Saves will be added for greater comfort.

notes.title: The Amazing American Circus review: I hate to say it, but there are better shows in town
notes.content:
By the time Henry Ford rolled up to see my show, I was ready to pack my trunk and say goodbye to the circus. I’d been ready a long time ago, truth be told, some time between inciting industrial action amongst JP Morgan’s workers and nabbing an automaton from Tesla. My troupe spread delight wherever we roamed, but the crowds weren’t to know we’d been plying the same tricks for hour after hour - nor that it had hardly taken one to hone my act to the point where failure was inconceivable. Every meagre juggling trick brought whoops from the crowd and impatience to my heart. With every high-wire act, my spirit sank lower still.

There’s no turn around coming, I’m afraid. The Amazing American Circus is a deckbuilder with some nice ideas, but it’s far more clown than strongman.

● During the Tutorial, you can see screens skipping, for example, the Show screen with the artists’ selection.

● After loading the game quests vanish from the journal. 
● After loading the game twice, quest markers disappear from the map screen and you can't complete active quests. 
● After finishing the game there appear End Credits and the game shuts down. After restarting the game we can press Continue, choose a game slot and continue the playthrough after getting 21 fame points. After another successful show it again shows End Credits and shuts down the game, but it can be re-loaded.

notes.title: Dev Blog #9
notes.content:
Hi All,

Before we get to the main attraction of this devblog... We are now [b]45% funded on Kickstarter[/b]! Please support us if you haven't yet (pledge, share, pretty please 🤡): https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/klabater/the-amazing-american-circus

You can’t have a good game without great music, and that’s a fact. Whether it’s an oldie and/or indie chiptune or a rock’n’roll riffing on the car radio in GTA or Cyberpunk, music is a must. That’s why for The Amazing American Circus we’ve teamed up with a fantastic Polish composer: [b]Patryk Scelina[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38997341/3aad12e7b07b18d3d63b403447ab99480067f9a8.jpg[/img]

Despite his young age, Patryk is a media and trailer music veteran, who’s built a sizable catalogue of music for one of the biggest publishing companies, BMG Production Music. His music has been used in multiple TV and Netflix productions, as well as video games, such as My Memory of Us - a previous game by the Juggler Games, Klabater’s partner in creation of The Amazing American Circus (you can get it when you choose some of the pledges!). Patryk’s soundtrack for My Memory of Us was appreciated by the Digital Dragons jury and nominated for Best Game Soundtrack. 

Check these two short samples from [i]TAAC[/i] recording sessions:

https://youtu.be/QidPiCRL1Ks
https://youtu.be/zFbVUEQS9G0

Music-wise, [i]The Amazing American Circus [/i]is a true challenge. Unlike many other games which need a specific type of sound or style, this one needs three: 

--> circus show tunes which require more conventional, classical march music
--> travelling soundtrack, inspired by traditional American folk music
--> dramatic, moving, and powerful score, to accentuate the plot-related feelings and emotions of the characters

According to Patryk, that latter is his favorite part. “[i]I wanted it to feel a bit more modern, while still keeping some obvious American folk influences. It is also not an easy task to make it work with a text-driven story.[/i]” 

As he points out, in case of a movie, a composer knows exactly when something happens. In a game such as The Amazing American Circus it’s the player who decides when to continue a conversation with another character. Because of that the music for these scenes has to be powerful, but also universal, to fit any moment. Patryk called it a puzzle but bravely took up the challenge. After all, that’s what game development is all about: challenging yourself and then reaping the rewards of your hard work.

‘till the next time!

notes.title: Graphical Update and... more!

Up until now the artists were facing left, towards the audience. It was a satisfying sight - the opponents are on the left and our artists on the right have to avoid their attacks. notes.title: DEV BLOG #8
notes.content:
In The Amazing American Circus, you’ll meet many characters, both historical and those known from American folklore. Some of them will become your friends; some will become your opponents who’ll try to stop you from becoming the most famous circus entrepreneur in the world. However, such chance encounters and bitter rivalries won’t work without a strong core of the main characters we wish to introduce today.

[b]Main hero[/b] - a young, 20-25 years old youngster, down on his luck, not sure what to do with his life, and seeking answers in drinking dens and on the road, going devil only knows where. One day, a chance for a change appears, though the protagonist receives a letter from his mother telling him about his father’s death in the grimmest of ways. They have never been close, but the main character immediately returns home. He learned that his father left him an unusual inheritance: an old, run-down, but still ready for the road circus. Has fate finally smiled upon our young hero? Is this what he’s been looking for all these years? A chance to turn his life around and become SOMEONE; someone respectable, who’ll make his mother proud and who’ll honor his father’s name. They may have been estranged for quite some time, but, well - family is family.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38997341/3dff77bcaf794dae9f4d16eeb391ca58b79147c0.jpg[/img]

[b]Father[/b] - the main hero’s father, Arthur Jones, was one of the most famous circus performers - once. The moment the older man kicks the proverbial bucket, his days of glory are long gone, and the once fabulous circus is to him nothing more than a pile of cloth and bitter memories. Like many other men, he tried to find answers at the bottom of a bottle of whiskey and a pint of upset, and like so many before him. He found nothing more than an endless hole where he kept falling and falling until he finally hit bottom and died. Still, in the last few months of his life, his biggest regret turned out not to be the fame he’d lost but the son he’d pushed away. Deep down, he always hoped his son would follow his footsteps and become an even more famous ringmaster than his old man. This is why he left the protagonist the circus - the only thing of value he’d ever had in his life.

[b]Mother[/b] - the main hero’s mother is a strong woman with a no-bullshit attitude. Beautiful and adventurous in her youth, she fell for the protagonist’s father - a slightly older but famous and wild circus performer. Still, a happily ever afterlife wasn’t meant for them. When they finally decided to settle down and have a child, they both left their best years far behind. Her husband was hardly ever home, trying to continue his career, spending all their money, but the older he got, the harder it was for him to keep up with the new, young, and talented circus artists. Finally, he gave up on his dream and joined his wife to live off of the small land they managed to get. But while she worked hard, he took to drinking; and while she blamed him for their misfortunes, he continued drinking. In the end, his death, though sad, was a relief to her - and a chance that maybe her son will become successful and take care of her - as a good child should.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38997341/f6bddbd4426fc34fc8c7e5e88f383680011456b5.jpg[/img]

[b]Uncle Jack[/b] - the protagonist’s uncle is an always drunk ne'er-do-well and a brother of the protagonist’s father. Once a famous circus performer, Jackie the High rope, was known across the country. But he too shared the fate of his brother, and they both lost fame and fortune and took to drinking, seeing no other future for them. Still, there was a difference in their approach to the new, and gloomy, life - while the protagonist’s father was becoming more and more miserable, uncle Jack was becoming more and more miserable… and hearty, and loud. Always happy to drink with anyone, be it a stranger or a friend, he managed to avoid the life of a hobo only thanks to the protagonist’s mother, who took pity on her brother-in-law and let him live with her. However, now, when the main hero inherits the once glorious circus, Jackie the High Rope sees it as a chance for him to return to the life he once had. And while he won’t be doing any tightrope walking, he intends to enjoy himself as much as he can, living - and drinking, of course - among young and glamorous artists.

notes.title: DEV BLOG #7
DEV BLOG #6
notes.content:
Have you ever heard about [i]Oregon Trail[/i] (1971)? It was an educational video game meant to show the hardships of traveling down the actual Oregon Trail, the over 2,000 miles road leading from the east of the USA to the then-still-wild west. It was a road used by many migrants seeking a new life - and by many adventurous to-be miners during the California Gold Rush.

Historical Oregon Trail was a road that was neither easy nor safe to cross, and that’s what the original game from 1971 showed with many events and quests that gamers had to face during their trip. In a way, some of the [i]Oregon Trail[/i] gameplay solutions were inherited by some game creators later. If you played games like, for example, [i]The Banner Saga[/i] series, you have definitely seen how the devs creatively approached this old concept.  More or less 50 years later, we decided to create another game showing the USA’s adventurous reality (also, it tells the story set more or less 50 years later than the original tale depicted in [i]Oregon Trail[/i]). Of course, unlike in the original Oregon Trail, we combine reality with fantasy; but still, this aged title is one of our main inspirations, and that’s where we get the idea of one of our main game mechanics: the events.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38997341/3e66ccb229e515f33e58fef86f0f1c348ffa39d8.jpg[/img]

The events are text-based pop-up windows telling you about an event that’s right now happening to or in your circus. They appear either during your venturing through the states or in town, where you set up your circus.

There are many types of events that can happen. An artist may get sick, or some food may be stolen; a strange man with an unusual request may approach you, or maybe the mayor of a small town will require the help of your circus. After all, given that your artists can soar through the air and lift trucks, there’s hardly a thing a circus is not capable of doing.

Each event brings choices. You may want to send a sick artist to a doctor, prepare some warm broth for them, or just tell them to stop whining and go back to training. Each choice comes with its outcome. Those usually bring something positive but may cost you another thing - it costs to heal an artist, but the poor soul might feel afterward better than ever. 

There are no choices that do not matter in the game. Through them, you create your story.

The events bring fortune and misfortune and require of you enough wit to choose what will be best for your circus troupe. It just might be worth it to help the orphans and to lose a lot of food if it increases the multiplier of the amount of fame you get; then again, it might be best at the given moment in time to lose fame and steal food from the orphans, just to make sure your artists survive another day on the road.

While most events are short messages, giving you 2-4 choices for different actions, some are dialogue-based. It may be a member of the audience astonished by your performance. It may be a drunken artist, asking you with tears in their eyes to help them get the girl. Thanks to that, you know that the circus and the world around it are alive, full of characters with their ways of speaking, emotions, needs, and desires.

Speaking of characters… You really can’t have a game set at the end of the 19th century without at least a few iconic characters from that era, both historical and fictional. You might want to have a drink in a dirty saloon with Pat Garrett. You might want to have Nicola Tesla build you a unique automaton for you to show around in your freakshow. The events and dialogues cover those too; you run into people on the road, they come to see your show; sometimes they might even be brought by a famous artist of yours, who seems to know just about everyone. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38997341/26244337c46f548b6a44d1b0a7489e4478fae705.png[/img]

Of course, most of the time, nothing’s free, and a given person has its character, needs, and opinions - but a few dollars, maybe a nice meal, a few compliments, or a short quest are often all that’s needed in this world to push forward and get what you want. There are options based on what your circus has to offer - a high level of a cooking cart allows you to provide a high-quality meal to a guest during many events. At the same time, a legendary artist is sure to step in at the right moment to save you from trouble by amazing a stranger with their act.

There are many types of events in the game, same as there are many genres and styles of stories that we’re drawing on. There are real moments, there are those that are epic and adventurous, but there are also those slightly less known, like Weird West and other subgenres of all that’s strange and otherworldly. 

No event’s the same - and every event pushes the story, your story, forward, in the direction you choose.

notes.title: DEV BLOG #5
notes.content:
Magical realism as we all know it is of course a style of fiction and literary genre that paints a realistic view of the modern world while also adding magical elements. We are pretty confident though, that it may as well apply to games! And we like to think that, in a way, [i]The Amazing American Circus[/i] is a game set in a magical realism environment. 

The end of the 19th century, the so-called Gilded Age, was not a great time to be alive. Sure, the economy was booming, the technology was evolving with each day, and clever inventors and slick businessmen were every day doing all they could to shape the new tomorrow.

But what about the rest of the folks? The poor farmers making their living on a barren land somewhere in the middle of nowhere, the immigrants working nearly 24/7 in factories, the frontiersmen with no new frontiers awaiting their conquest? For them there was no gold in Gilded; there was hardly any other color than the greyness of their harsh reality.

But then there was the CIRCUS...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38997341/b5b1562c36f5fcfe68c460e6ce541e5d5a692b1d.png[/img]

The circus brought lights and laughter and music, glamour, art, and magic. The circus was it’s own little pocket universe, with its own laws, both those governing the people and those of nature - even the laws of gravity couldn’t affect the artists soaring high in the air of the big top. The circus brought the essence of what dreams and fairytales are made of - but it was real. That was its beauty; for a few moments, you could leave the harsh reality behind and touch the magic.

The juxtaposition of these two things, the harsh reality, and the fairy-tale magic is the basis for the atmosphere of [i]The Amazing American Circus[/i]. The world is a tough place to live in and there might be danger lurking behind every corner. Someone might break into your cart and steal food or money; no money and food mean angry and hungry artists, and badly performing artists mean a circus on the brink of falling apart. 

But every bad thing has its opposite good thing too. Even a hungry Illusionist might astonish the audience, same as an angry Snake Charmer might still charm the audience. In the end, it all depends on your skills and whether you manage to carve yourself a path through the harsh reality. After all, this is the circus - it has its own rules. And after all - this is an adventure; your adventure.

So, how about following the rumors about a bigfoot living in the nearby mountains? Your freakshow sure could use such a famous critter. And how about helping that strange man planning a train heist? You do have a genius counting chicken, it might be capable of cracking a safe code in no time...
Of course, the audience doesn’t care about your adventures. They didn’t come here to listen to your stories about the fantastic times you’ve had, no. In fact, many of them traveled hundreds of miles, just to see your circus perform! And all the time they have is just a few hours…

So, don’t be surprised if the people on the bleachers don’t seem too happy to be there at the beginning of the show. They are tired, they are disgruntled, they see the world as a tough, unwelcoming place. But they want you to change that. Sure, they might throw a tomato at you or two; normally, an artist has to suffer for their art. What matters is that by the end of the show, when they’re leaving the big top, there are smiles on their faces - smiles that will remain there no matter how hard is the work they have to return to. 

And while they return to work, your own job in the given place is done - and the dusty trail awaits you, and with it many more fantastic adventures.

In this mix of reality and magic, you’ll see it all: cowboys and genius inventors; your biggest fans and your greatest enemies; strange lights in the sky and even stranger creatures hiding in the thicket by the side of the road; small ghost towns and huge metropolises.

The circus performance is like a day-dream - it cuts into the harsh reality, puts a smile on one’s face - and then it’s gone, in a blink of an eye.

notes.title: DEV BLOG #4
notes.content:
[i]Oh, I've killed men in Georgia,
And men in Alabam'
But kill a man in Arkansas
And God your soul will damn...[/i]

Cowboys. There's hardly a more famous image when one thinks about the Wild West than a cowboy riding through the prairie on their horse, preferably towards the setting sun, towards the unknown; after all, a cowboy is always on the road.

The story of [i]The Amazing American Circus[/i] begins in the west of the United States, at the end of the 19th century. The times were turbulent then, with robber barons fighting for land and riches, people fighting for their rights, different ethnicities clashing – but among all that there were cowboys, unmoved by the chaos around them. After all, a cowboy needs nothing more than his gun, a trusty steed, and maybe a golden shot – or a full bottle, preferably – of whiskey somewhere in a dirty saloon, in a small, rough town with a cool name, like Tombstone, or Deadwood. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38997341/04ca7a1eca8642c54b21e4c70359467fd56a7569.png[/img]

While [i]The Amazing American Circus[/i] is not a pure western game, it will take you to the west of the United States; the Wild West that was nearing its end as fast as the new age was approaching. Still, it was a place full of famous people, sharpshooters, outlaws, and sheriffs, and hell, who knows – maybe you'll even see a high-noon shootout or bump into another circus claiming that the small town you've entered is not big enough for the two of you.

And while our game is not focused on cowboys, you are sure to bump into one or two of them on the ol' dusty trail. Heck, after all, even Buffalo Bill, a famous gunslinger, had his own show and traveled across the States, just like you, seeking fame, glory, and adoration of the people.
So, without further ado, here are some of the famous cowboys - and cowgirls - you just might find yourself coming across in the game:

[b]William Frederick Cody[/b], better known as Buffalo Bill. A Pony Express rider, a soldier, a bison hunter turned showman, he managed to gain so much fame during his lifetime that his Wild West Show toured the United States and even Great Britain, and the whole of Europe. But how will he react to meeting a young circus owner rising to fame – and thus becoming his competitor? There's a chance that you won't be able to leave the west behind unless you show the folks which one of you is the real deal...

[b]Annie Oakley[/b], a sharpshooter extraordinaire, capable of shooting corks off of wine bottles and cigars out of her husband’s teeth (a great – and very Wild West – way to convince someone to stop smoking!), she was a good friend to the Native American leader, Sitting Bull, with whom she performed in Buffalo Bill's shows. But whose side will she choose? Her employer or maybe our young hero trying to make a name for himself?

[b]Pat Garrett[/b]. There's probably not a single more famous Wild West outlaw than Billy the Kid, and there's perhaps not a single more famous lawman than the man who shot him down. So remember to buy him a drink when you run into him and maybe he'll tell you his tale and he might even ask you for help if he's impressed enough by your circus performance. After all, there's a limit to what a gunslinger can do – but the skills of your artists and the magic of the circus have no end.

[b]Wyatt Earp[/b]. Another famous sheriff, and the man who took part in the most famous shootouts – the Gunfight at the O.K. Corral in Tombstone, Arizona. Lawmen against outlaws, in a town that was most certainly not big enough for all of them. But what is the good ol' Wyatt up to nowadays? Well, you just might find out; maybe in a small saloon in the middle of nowhere – or maybe he'll come to you himself, having heard of your amazing circus.

[b]Martha Jane Cannary[/b], better known as Calamity Jane, was a wild and challenging (how else can you get a nickname 'Calamity'?) frontierswoman, who took part in numerous military campaigns. She saw it all – the most remote parts of the west, the most famous and dangerous towns. But there's a high chance – as high as noon is when two cowboys duel – that she's never seen a circus performance. How will you fare when such a – literal – calamity enters the bleachers and expects to be amazed?

These are just some of the cowboys and cowgirls you'll meet in the game. Some you'll befriend, some you'll fight, and some will pay you no mind at all unless you impress them with your skills. Remember that a circus is a rare thing in the Wild West, and the magic, the lights, and the beauty of it are sure to attract many a folk, no matter their background, profession, or creed.

It's hard to tell where the dusty trail will take you, but you'll be fine – just remember to always follow that setting sun...

notes.title: DEV BLOG #3
notes.content:
American history is all about being in constant motion, being on the road...

In the early 19th Century, the United States was a new, developing country with settlers steadily pushing the American frontier… The US history is full of stories related to iconic trails and roads people had to follow to pursue happiness, fortune, or whatever dream they had. Sometimes they just run from their past. We all heard about The Pony Express Trail, where young men on horseback once carried the nation’s mail across the country from 1860-1861. Later, those ‘trails’ took the form of iconic routes like the legendary Road 66, glorified in countless songs, books, and movies. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38997341/cb4a90fc55e311651e7281934e9b32f6dd9b70cf.png[/img]

To reach their public at the time, Circus showmen had little choice but to travel light and fast. In [i][b]The Amazing American Circus[/b][/i], you will visit legendary places and meet real historical characters being a part of the American circus heritage. You will plan your trip and adapt your artistic offer to different groups of spectators in a constant struggle to provide hard-working Americans with the entertainment they deserve! In a way, [i][b]The Amazing American Circus[/b][/i] is a gaming answer to the classic ‘road movies’ genre. Emerge from the South West and reach the progressive North East while seeking fame, glory, and fortune! What’s more, ‘American’ than that?

In [i][b]The Amazing American Circus[/b][/i], the game map will is e divided into 4 regions. Northeast and West being the permanent element of the game’s walkthrough, and Midwest and South being optional routes to take. -You will choose which direction he or she wants to follow during narrative events. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38997341/ae28d4bb95c3c01ccae6cd1a765c7d36e5f71a50.png[/img]

Each region will bring a unique value and vibe both gameplay-wise and in the narrative:

[list]
[*] [b]West[/b] will be ‘Wild’ indeed with a narrative focus on Native Americans’ mythology and system of beliefs. West part of the USA was the last to be fully colonized and a very tough turf for Circus performers as the audience here will be demanding and often unforgiving. To make things even worse, you will start there! 
[*] You will immediately notice that you have entered [b]the Midwest[/b] thanks to the lower temperatures and lots of weird-looking trappers all around you;). You will also encounter miners, tough folk, and even a stricter type of audience. Entertain them, and you can call yourself a Circus pro!
[*] [b]South[/b] is all about folklore, voodoo, and swamps. Expect the unexpected here. Not everything you see here is real!
[*] [b]Northeast[/b] - New England and neighboring territories. In theory, this is a modern America you want to be a part of, with a stylish audience spending heck of a lot of money! But in reality? It is a brutal battleground between the key Circus players and a place where the final Circus fight with P.T Barnum himself awaits you…
[/list]

Initially, the US map is covered by a ‘fog of war’ and, besides the narrative events and milestones, you are relatively free to choose your path. Your main goal is to give performances in various towns, but you may perform a lot of other activities on the map. The type of settlement will somewhat indicate what kind of action or adventure may await you there. As for the types of settlements, we distinguish the following:

[list]
[*] Small Town
[*] Farming Village 
[*] Mining Settlement  
[*] Modern industrial City 
[*] State Capitals
[*] Military Camps
[*] Indian Reservations
[/list]
Each type of settlement will also feature different crowds. It does not mean that you will only meet miner folk in mining settlements, but you may, of course, expect to encounter miners while visiting the mine:) 

Before you hit the road, you need to choose the desired destination and the type of food resources for the planned trip (we will tell you more about Food in one of the upcoming blogs). What is essential, you may assign specific types of food to individual artists to ensure they gain definite perks, which add some depth into planning and tactics. What’s more, some narrative events may affect your trip’s speed, so it is wise to gather more supplies as it may turn out that you need more Food to reach the selected destination. If you ignore the supply chain’s preparation, you can still travel, but your Artists will suffer from many negative perks and debuff effects… 

During your travels on the map screen, you will notice time passing by, symbolized by a Circus wagon moving on an animated background. If you have played Banner Saga, you probably remember the caravan traveling through the land. It looks pretty similar in The Amazing American Circus. 

On this screen, it is also possible to activate random narrative events. You may meet some strangers or even hire new performers! You may also chat with the so-called legendary artists employed in your troupe during your adventures. Some of them will have something exciting or useful to say in certain regions. 

So, while [b][i]The Amazing American Circus[/i][/b] is mostly a strategy, simulation, and a card game, this ‘road movie’ feeling is heavily present in the gameplay’s backbone. We do hope you will enjoy traveling across weird America!

notes.title: DEV BLOG #2
notes.content:
Welcome to the second episode of [i]The Amazing American Circus[/i] dev blog! Today we would like to shed more light on the ‘fighting’ mechanics featured in our game along with general info about the audience you may encounter during your travel. 

Important note, since our game does not include any real and brutal encounters, by ‘fight’ we mean your circus show! Who is the enemy then? 

Here’s the first catch; your biggest enemy is your audience... Sounds strange? Not necessary, if you think of the crowds visiting circuses and theatres back in the 19th and early 20th centuries:) In those days, Circus was one of the not-so-many entertainment choices, and it attracted a somewhat different audience than today. There are even historical reports of violent behavior among the public during the shows. We do not include any of these events in the game yet (maybe we will!), but the whole idea of the audience being your enemy (isn’t that SO cool, punk rock and all?) seemed charming, and we decided to make it an essential part of the gameplay.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38997341/ae7fc381e23a87163a917c2822add0feae73bafc.jpg[/img]

In [i]The Amazing American Circus[/i], you will visit varied locations, be it large towns or small, provincial countrysides. You will deliver your show to both aristocrats and simple folk, among them rowdy workers or bored troublemakers. And who you will meet during each performance, will heavily affect your gameplay options. 

[b]Your worst fear is the audience's indifference. Your best weapon is a dazzling amusement. Your artists are your army. [/b]

And now for the ‘fighting’ basics (We will discuss further details in upcoming episodes of our dev blog):

Since [i]The Amazing American Circus[/i] is, above all else, a card game in a similar fashion to, let’s say, Slay the Spire, ‘fighting’ your Audience is based on card battling mechanics.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38997341/fd04a2abead715146aced0ae2969127dcda0f856.gif[/img]

At the beginning of each show/encounter, the player chooses five cards from the previously acquired deck (you gather cards through attending narrative events, exploring the map, and delivering outstanding performances). We call it the [b]‘Hand’ deck[/b], these five cards will be the opening of the ‘fight’. What’s more, five doesn’t have to be necessary for the final number in every encounter. Some factors may affect it, like the following:

[list]
[*] previous choices and events
[*] buffs and debuffs
[*] active perks 
[*] finisher’s effects
[*] chosen performers’ unique abilities
[*] Results related to the dishes served in your Circus Camp
[/list]
Along with the ‘Hand’ deck comes a refill of the[b] ‘Charisma’[/b] meter required to play the selected cards and in many ways affecting the whole encounter. This factor may also be subject to some changes and positive/negative effects influencing your show. 

As a player, you decide which cards you want to play and when. You just chose the card, drag & drop it on a selected Audience member (each having their own abilities and pers as well, so choose wisely!). You may also play the ‘neutral’ card by dragging and dropping it in the middle of the screen with no particular Spectators or Artist in mind. Neutral cards usually have a sweeping effect on the show. Before you choose any of the cards, you may, of course, check their impacts, and as we do have around 170 cards in the game, there’’s a lot of planning and checking waiting for you here;) After you play each card, it, of course, lands in the pile of ‘used’ cards.  

It’s too early to reveal full details but not every card can be played every time. Sometimes you need to fill the Charisma meter or pay a special cost for playing individual cards. When you use all the cards, your turn is over. 

Most of the cards in your deck are related to certain artists you invite to your troupe. So, the more artist you hire, the more choices you have. Not only you may select a specific set of performers before each show (it is a significant choice related to the type of the Audience you are about to encounter), but you may also choose between cards linked to them. 

So, overall, there is a considerable strategy and tactics field for correct planning and executing. [b]Each artist has five cards at his disposal[/b], i.e. concrete acrobatic tricks or illusionist hoaxes, etc. And, as we choose three artists for each show, [b]that gives the player 15 cards to play[/b]. 

At the beginning of each turn, the player draws more cards from the overall Deck chosen for individual encounters, and so it goes until the final of the given show. If you don’t have enough cards at your disposal (i.e., you lost some due to the enemy’s buff), the game will randomly draw cards from your used cards pile. But, hold on, this not goes without penalty. Drawing cards from the used cards pile may cost your performers additional stress and affect their statistics.

So, these are, already pretty complicated, basics. We will share more details in upcoming episodes of our dev blog. Make sure you shoot us in the comments should you have any questions!

notes.title: DEVBLOG #1
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38997341/b9da5fb6f432e80d33f84fef0b43f75f75ed663b.gif[/img]

Hello Spectators!

As this is our first Dev Blog post, we thought it’s a good idea to explain our inspirations. The setting of our game is pretty unique, so it is probably worth a while to give you heads-up about the original idea. 

First of all, we love tycoons,  we play tons of them, but as fans, we still have this feeling that most of them are missing some crucial ‘narrative’ components. We did a decent research some time ago, and our conclusion was as follows: three key elements would make tycoons much more appealing: [b]a deepened narrative[/b] with [b]RPG[/b], and [b]simulation[/b] elements included. So, in a way, we have invented this Narrative RPG tycoon genre! 

We have implemented some of these conclusions in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/867290/Crossroads_Inn_Anniversary_Edition/]Crossroads Inn[/url] game we have released in 2019. We have learned a lot while working on this ambitious project and decided to follow this path with our next game. And this next title is, as you can imagine, The Amazing American Circus! These two are of course a slightly different breed, but there are many common ideas in approach to gameplay and story-telling. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38997341/64e4c56f8cc0dbfabb10b4cce034ac2d0e8c81de.jpg[/img]

Why Circus? And why an American Circus? Well, it all started with this [url=https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/americanexperience/films/circus/]excellent documentary by PBS[/url] we spotted on Netflix. After watching it, we immediately felt this is a perfect theme for a video game! There are only a few games out there about Circus, while this setting has so much to offer! Vivid characters, spirited performances, and generous, sometimes funny, sometimes sad stories of circus artists. This vintage, somewhat magical form of entertainment gives a lot of o possibilities to create cool gameplay mechanics.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38997341/24caa46edb8c5c41663b01262be17bc509eedb59.gif[/img]

So, in The Amazing American Circus, we will tell you a story of the most iconic entertainment in American history. The USA, during the Gilded Age, is a turbulent place. On the East Coast springs up a modern metropolis, while in the west, cowboys and robber barons fight for their business. The new era is coming, and this is the last right moment for the Circus to flourish!

Gameplaywise, we were inspired by the most fantastic card game there – [b]Slay the Spire[/b]! The Amazing American Circus's essential part is collecting a deck of cards, playing them wisely against the audience, and finding the best strategies throughout the game to create the best performance.
The second important element is exploration! In our game, you will travel across the United States, visiting towns and villages from West to East, searching for cash and glory. During your trip, you will recruit various performers, meet real historical figures, and face challenges of unprecedented scale. While designing this particular element, we had a famous [b]Sid Meier's Pirates[/b] in the back of our heads but also the good old [b]Oregon Trail[/b]!

Finally, the third crucial gameplay pillar is the management of your troupe and circus camp – here, we thought the Darkest Dungeon is the best benchmark. You will need to recruit performers, cope with their demands and needs, manage the resources, and upgrade your Circus.
So if You fancy this exotic blend of features, then please stay tuned with us for more DevBlogs coming soon, as the show must go on!

notes.title: The Amazing American Circus Announced!
notes.content:
Klabater, a developer of Crossroads Inn, and Juggler Games - studio behind My Memory of Us, have announced their new collaborative production - The Amazing American Circus. The game is set to be released on PC and consoles in 2021.

Watch the announcement teaser: https://youtu.be/JYf6bnOrLI8

The Amazing American Circus is a unique blend of a card game, tycoon, and an adventure game. Build a wandering circus, collect a strong deck of cards, gather a fantastic troupe of artists and performers, and travel across the 19th century United States! Dare to challenge the legendary P.T. Barnum and make your enterprise the most incredible show of America!

"At Klabater, we are fascinated by history. We develop and publish narrative-driven games that depict vital and thought-provoking moments in life. We are currently focusing on the turbulent times of the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The Amazing American Circus marks a bold third chapter in our ambitious project of games that combine captivating narratives from that era with eye-catching art and compelling gameplay. The best-selling games We. The Revolution and Help Will Come Tomorrow were the first two chapters." - Said Michal Gembicki, CEO at Klabater.

[b]Your worst fear is the audience's indifference. Your best weapon is a dazzling amusement. Your artists are your army. Behold, the circus came to town![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38997341/64e4c56f8cc0dbfabb10b4cce034ac2d0e8c81de.jpg[/img]

The Amazing American Circus tells the story of the most iconic entertainment in American history. The USA, during the Gilded Age, is a turbulent place with serious social problems and rapid economic growth with railroads and industrialization leading the way. On the East Coast, a modern metropolis springs up, while in the west, cowboys and robber barons and farmers battle for a piece of the new American dream… A new era is coming, and it may be the right moment for a traveling circus to flourish. 

“The Amazing American Circus blends our unique artistic vision with meticulous gameplay design.” said Lukasz Janczuk from Juggler Games. “My Memory of Us was an important story of two kids escaping an oppressive system through varied logical puzzles. With The Amazing American Circus we want to offer an exotic world of pioneer entertainers, alongside a challenging card game and enjoyable management system.”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38997341/4ba37c5642e8041cfc022074d0856fbcf14dd930.jpg[/img]

You take the role of an impoverished owner of a traveling Circus. Through your personal and multithreaded story, The Amazing American Circus reveals mysteries behind a uniquely American form of entertainment.
Deliver a perfect show in a special card duel between you and the audience. Boredom is your enemy, and your performances and tricks are your best weapons. Choose your cards wisely and try to figure out the mood of the crowd. As a traveling Circus owner, you need to look for new troupe members. During your travels, you will try to gather an exotic crew of performers, but can you deliver the best shows, win the audience’s approval, or will you fail? 

A unique story filled with love affairs, hateful enemies, and magnificent shows with challenging audiences and quests, all of this wrapped up in a writing style that resembles the dime novels from the turn of the 20th century - that's what The Amazing American Circus offers. 

What The Amazing American Circus has to offer?
[list]
[*] Save a run-down circus, gather a troupe of performers, and dare to defy the greatest showman on earth - P.T Barnum himself.
[*] Enjoy an original and challenging card game. You will battle against your greatest enemies, audience boredom, and stagnation.
[*] Gather a group of extraordinary artists and twisted individuals, each with their own story to tell, and journey across the 19th century United States.
[*] Indulge in a story set in the turbulent times of the Industrial Revolution and the dusk of the Wild West era, and dive into the beautiful and grim world of the American folklore
[*] 100+ real historical and legendary characters from the verge of the 19th and 20th century to encounter, such as John D. Rockefeller, Susan B. Anthony, or Nikola Tesla.
[*] Experience an epic soundtrack inspired by classical circus music
[/list]
The Amazing American Circus will be released in 2021. Please visit the [url=https://www.facebook.com/AACircusGame]Facebook page[/url] for more information.
